interpretation: This study measures whether a benchmark's SCORING PIPELINE (answer extractor, LLM judge, rubric grader, or unit-test verifier) can be gamed by answers that a machine oracle proves wrong, and whether iterated repair of that scorer converges. It does NOT claim: that a model is generally weak or strong; that a benchmark is worthless; balanced model comparison; human agreement; or that exploits reflect typical deployment behavior beyond the reported natural-incidence (L0) rung. Causal-slice claims are made only from factorial cells (procedural or witnessed-universe forks); observational metadata clusters are labeled hypothesis-generating.

program.thesis: an evaluation must prove its own validity before any score counts

responsible_disclosure.policy: coordinated disclosure with a suggested patch before public release
